classification_signals: Chapter 4: RESEARCH METHODOLOGY details 'multiple data collection methods' including 'questionnaire and spatial analysis' and 'systematic observation' (page 167).
Reports quantitative results from 300 questionnaires per district and statistical analyses (Mann Whitney U test, Kruskal Wallis test) (pages 168, 194-196, 233).
Presents cognitive maps and their analysis (pages 184-207).
Chapter 5: TERRITORIAL FUNCTIONING IN THE CASE OF KAVAKLIDERE AND ÇUKURAMBAR DISTRICTS IN ANKARA presents empirical findings.
title: HUMAN TERRITORIAL FUNCTIONING AT THE SCALE OF RESIDENTIAL ENVIRONMENTS

findings.consequent: Cognitive, emotional, and moral development of individuals
findings.quote: contact with the near home environment is still important for the cognitive, emotional, and moral development of individuals.

findings.antecedent: Lack of spatial control, diminishing sense of community, alienation
findings.consequent: Problems in contemporary cities
findings.quote: contemporary cities with the problems of loss of spatial control, diminishing sense of community and alienation.

findings.consequent: Place attachment, understanding/regulating man-environment relations, spatial regulation, social organization
findings.quote: concept of 'territoriality', which can be utilized in both understanding and regulating man-environment relations, emerges as one of the premise spatial behaviors that strengthen place attachment.

findings.consequent: Cognitive, emotional, and moral development of individuals, sense of self, orientation to the world, tie to social world
findings.quote: attachment to particular places has been asserted as a very vital part of cognitive, emotional, and moral development of individuals

findings.consequent: Acquaintances and connecting with other people
findings.quote: residing location is still a determinant factor for acquaintances and connecting with other people

findings.antecedent: Loss of clear boundaries between public and private territories, lack of interface zones, inappropriate distribution of public territory
findings.consequent: Lack of spatial control, identity deficiencies, sustainability deficiencies, security deficiencies, lack of places for attachment
findings.quote: loss of clear boundaries between public and private territories, lack of interface zones... resulting in the lack of places that people can attach to.

findings.consequent: Crime, control/defense of environment, sense of belonging, security
findings.quote: environmental design and sense of territoriality can reduce crime and motivate people to control and defend their own environment and enhance their sense of belonging and security

findings.antecedent: High rates of urbanization, decreasing familiarity with environment, alienation, safety problems, pollution, car dominance
findings.consequent: High levels of stress for urban dwellers
findings.quote: urban dwellers are now facing high levels of stress resulting from high rates of urbanization, decreasing familiarity with the environment and people residing at the same place (alienation), safety problems, pollution, car dominance over streets etc.

findings.antecedent: Transformation in residential development patterns (facility-based to home-based, continuous fabric to cellular developments like gated communities/mass housing)
findings.consequent: Shifts in territoriality of urban residents
findings.quote: transformation in residential development patterns from facility-based to home-based; continuous fabric as in the traditional neighborhoods to cellular developments... also caused shifts in terms of territoriality of urban residents.

findings.consequent: Cramped spaces, stressful behaviors, relationships, emotional outlets
findings.quote: It is then possible to conceive that people can be cramped by the spaces in which they have to live and work. They may even find themselves forced into behaviors, relationships or emotional outlets that are overly stressful.

findings.antecedent: Absence of a good neighborhood environment
findings.consequent: Exclusion of less advantaged groups from socio-economic life of the city
findings.quote: the absence of a good neighborhood environment may result in even more exclusion of less advantaged groups from the socio-economic life of the city.

findings.antecedent: Squeezing residential functions into home limits, delineating territory without human scale/territorial needs, recent developments in residential areas (private dwellings in vast public lands, no intermediary zone)
findings.consequent: Bad replica of radical modernist visions, erosion of semi-public domain
findings.quote: squeezing residential functions into the limits of the home, thus delineating a territory without taking into account human scale or territorial needs, the recent developments in residential areas also form an image of a bad replica of the radical modernist visions.

findings.antecedent: Private domain taking role of old neighborhoods (well-equipped homes, social interactions within single building), commercial/services transferred to city scale
findings.consequent: Erosion of semi-public domain
findings.quote: the private domain takes on the role of the old neighborhoods and functions as a local group territory... while commercial and other services maintained at the neighborhood scale are also transferred to the city scale. Hence, it can be claimed that the change in the way urban residential environments are designed with the changing role of the private domain resulted in the erosion of the semi-public domain

findings.antecedent: New neighborhoods (gated communities, mass housing) sustained by perceived similarities in lifestyle (consumption, cultural cues)
findings.consequent: Imaginary communities, limited unknown experience/encounters with strangers, questioning values/identities, social segregation, alienation
findings.quote: new neighborhoods’... are made up of ‘imaginary communities’ which are sustained by perceived similarities in life-style... limit the unknown experience and encounters with strangers... which may force residents to question their values and identities

findings.antecedent: Lack of appropriation of space by residents in new residential developments
findings.consequent: Lack of sense of territoriality
findings.quote: the new residential developments are lacking a sense of territoriality in terms of appropriation of space by its residents.

findings.antecedent: Appropriation of near-home territories by residents (creating semi-public, semi-private zones)
findings.consequent: Development of local social networks, security issues
findings.quote: appropriation of near-home territories by residents creating semi-public, semi-private zones is set as essential both for the development of local social networks and security issues

findings.consequent: Place attachment, feelings of identity, security, stimulation
findings.quote: sense of territoriality can foster place attachment and the feelings of identity; security and stimulation within these environments

findings.consequent: Psychological, social-psychological, and social-ecological outcomes
findings.quote: human territorial functioning has psychological, social – psychological as well as social-ecological (Taylor, 1988) outcomes.

findings.antecedent: Territoriality (laying claim, communicating ownership, exclusive use, definable physical space, perceived/actual ownership)
findings.consequent: Regulation of social interactions (privacy, interaction), enhanced sense of identity, feeling of competence (familiarity), promoted feeling of security, stimulation (marking, modifying, defending)
findings.quote: territoriality... helps to regulate social interactions (by providing both privacy and interaction), enhance the sense of identity and feeling of competence through familiarity with the environment, promote the feeling of security and provide stimulation through marking, modifying and defending that territory.

findings.antecedent: Different designs of the environment (territorial organization of space)
findings.consequent: Different territorialities (territorial functioning)
findings.quote: the results of the empirical study also reveal that different designs of the environment (territorial organization of space) reveal different territorialities.

findings.antecedent: Contemporary residential environments ('enclaves', gated communities) vs. traditional urban residential environments (continuous fabric, 'walking distance neighborhoods')
findings.consequent: Divergence in territorial functioning (cognitive and behavior patterns)
findings.quote: territorial functioning in terms of both cognitive and behavior patterns diverge between contemporary residential environments organized in the form of ‘enclaves’... and traditional urban residential environments... with continuous fabric that are organized similar to ‘walking distance neighborhoods’.

findings.consequent: Conceive residential living spaces as meaningful territorial units, demarcate boundaries, identify landmarks and activity nodes
findings.quote: residents are able to define the subjective boundaries of their residential territory. Besides, the majority of the respondents were able to mention at least one landmark in their area. Yet, the results also show that respondents actively use their residential territory as an exclusive resource base mainly for commercial and recreational functions. In this regard, it can be claimed that respondents in both cases conceive their residential territory as a meaningful territorial unit.

findings.consequent: Rather unique (lack of consensus on boundaries)
findings.quote: it cannot be claimed that there is a consensus among residents on the boundaries of the territory since subjective boundaries defined by the respondents are rather unique.

findings.antecedent: Shared core area (agreed by residents), types of activities, mode of transportation
findings.consequent: High degrees of consensus
findings.quote: a shared core agreed by the residents with high degrees of consensus is depicted in both cases. Additionally, there is also high amounts of consensus on the types of activities as well as the mode of transportation to reach these activities for the residents of the same residential territory.

findings.antecedent: Territorial organization of space (territorial depth, affordances), individual/social-group characteristics of residents
findings.consequent: Differences in territorial functioning (cognition and behavior)
findings.quote: territorial functioning of urban residents differs with respect to both territorial organization of space (including territorial depth and affordances of the environment) as well as the individual and social-group characteristics of the residents.

findings.consequent: Perceived as prominent elements in bounding residential territories
findings.quote: major roads are perceived as the prominent elements in bounding the residential territories in the recent era.

findings.antecedent: Major roads with heavy car traffic
findings.consequent: Less permeable elements, separators rather than boundaries (connecting territory to adjacent territories)
findings.quote: major roads are less permeable elements in terms of connecting the territory to adjacent territories thus becoming separators rather than boundaries.

findings.consequent: Smaller perceived residential territory (walking distance scale)
findings.quote: respondents from traditional urban residential environments (as in the case of Kavaklıdere) tend to perceive smaller units which connotes to a walking distance scale

findings.consequent: Larger perceived residential territory (driving distance scale)
findings.quote: respondents from contemporary residential environments (as in the case of Çukurambar) tend to perceive larger areas as their residential territory that connotes to a driving distance scale.

findings.consequent: Often do not match administrative boundaries
findings.quote: the boundaries designated by the respondents do not often match with the administrative boundaries.

findings.consequent: Average perceived boundaries similar to administrative boundaries of neighborhoods
findings.quote: the average size of the perceived boundaries is more similar to the size of the administrative boundaries of the neighborhoods in Kavaklıdere district

findings.consequent: Average designated boundaries smaller than administrative boundaries of neighborhoods
findings.quote: in Çukurambar the average designated boundaries are rather smaller than the administrative boundaries of the neighborhoods. Hence, the subdivision of urban areas into smaller spatial (residential) units by planners falls short in explaining the territorial extent of the residential environment.

findings.antecedent: Shared core areas in Kavaklıdere and Çukurambar
findings.consequent: Dominantly commercial functions
findings.quote: the shared core areas of both in Kavaklıdere and Çukurambar districts contains dominantly commercial functions.

findings.consequent: Absence of public spaces
findings.quote: the absence of public spaces at the shared core of the residential environments is also an issue which planning interventions shall focus.

findings.consequent: Tend to refer mainly to buildings as landmarks, least to open spaces
findings.quote: in terms of landmarks individuals tend to refer mainly to buildings and least to open spaces in both cases.

findings.consequent: Lack legible public open spaces that can be referred as landmarks, inadequate distribution of open public territories
findings.quote: both traditional and contemporary residential environment lack legible public open spaces that can be referred as landmarks which put forth the inadequate distribution of open public territories in residential environments.

findings.consequent: Diminishing number of streets referred as landmarks by respondents
findings.quote: street names are given numerically rather than by actual names in Çukurambar results in the diminishing number of streets referred as landmarks by the respondents.

findings.antecedent: Territorial gaps (fear/discomfort zones delimited by respondents)
findings.consequent: Directly impacts everyday experience of residents, important part of territorial cognition
findings.quote: territorial gaps... are important part of territorial cognition at the residential scale which directly impacts the everyday experience of the residents.

findings.antecedent: Non-residential uses creating infrastructural problems (parking, noise, crowding), vacant lots, construction sites
findings.consequent: Prominent types of territorial gaps in residential territories
findings.quote: non-residential uses creating infrastructural problems such as parking as well as noise and crowding and vacant lots and construction sites are the prominent types of territorial gaps in residential territories.

findings.antecedent: Total activity (number of activities done within the district)
findings.consequent: Satisfaction from the residential area (Çukurambar)
findings.quote: low positive correlation between total activity and satisfaction scores (r = 0,206; p <0,001) in Çukurambar

findings.consequent: Perceived residential area size (Kavaklıdere)
findings.quote: low-level positive correlation between the number of landmarks and the perceived residential area size (r = 0,177; p <0,01) in Kavaklıdere

findings.consequent: Differences in territorial functioning at the residential scale
findings.quote: the spatial organization of space is a prominent factor causing the differences in territorial functioning at the residential scale.

findings.antecedent: Loss of intermediary zones (erosion of semi-public domain), larger distances, impermeable boundary mechanisms (Çukurambar)
findings.consequent: Larger perceived residential territory (driving distance scale), lack of defensibility of space, less 'eyes on the street', decreased ability to use near home environments, car-dependency
findings.quote: loss of intermediary zones between the public and private territories, in other words erosion of semi-public domain, resulting from both the larger distances as well as impermeable boundary mechanisms in the territorial organization of space in the case of Çukurambar can be linked with both the larger perceived size of the residential territory (driving distance scale) since there is a lack of defensibility of space, less number of eyes on the street and when combined with the narrow sidewalks decrease the ability of the residents to actively use their near home environments and also to car-dependency while using the residential territory as a resource base.

findings.antecedent: Passive intermediary zones between public and private territories
findings.consequent: Decreased probability of social interaction, smaller number of central markers (private/public), place attachment not attained
findings.quote: passive intermediary zones between the public and private territories also decreases the probability of social interaction at this scale which also results in the smaller number of central markers both at the private and public spaces since place attachment cannot be attained with the near home environment.

findings.antecedent: Active/passive character of interface zones, proximity/permeability of boundary markers
findings.consequent: Quality of lived space
findings.quote: active or passive character of these interface zones between the public and private territories and proximity and permeability of boundary markers used in each territory is an important parameter affecting the quality of the lived space.

findings.consequent: Variances in territorial functioning (cognitive and behavioral levels)
findings.quote: societal factors both at the social group and individual scales creates variances in territorial functioning both at the cognitive and behavioral levels.

findings.consequent: Less effective on territorial functioning than affordances of the environment
findings.quote: societal factors are less effective on territorial functioning than affordances of the environment.

findings.consequent: As important as accessibility for reaching activities/facilities (especially for older populations)
findings.quote: propinquity is as important as accessibility in terms of reaching activities and facilities at the residential scale especially for the older populations.

findings.antecedent: Variety of functions within and at close proximity to the district
findings.consequent: Facilitative impact on behavior of residents (exclusive use of residential territory as resource base)
findings.quote: existence of a variety of functions within and at a close proximity to the district has a facilitative impact on behavior of residents in terms of exclusive use of residential territory as a resource base.

findings.antecedent: Services/facilities further away than catchment areas (proposed in theory/practice)
findings.consequent: Included in residents' cognitive maps as located within residential territory, actively used
findings.quote: services and facilities that are further away than the catchment areas proposed in theory and practice are included in the resident’s cognitive maps as located within their residential territory and actively used by the respondents.

findings.antecedent: Buffer zone at periphery of residential territory
findings.consequent: Regarded as an exclusive base for higher needs of urban residents (rather than simple catchment area analysis for basic needs)
findings.quote: buffer zone at the periphery of the residential territory can also be regarded as an exclusive base for higher needs of the urban residents rather than simple catchment area analysis for basic needs.

findings.antecedent: Higher number of central markers (individual private territory, collective public territory) in Kavaklıdere
findings.consequent: Higher degrees of place attachment and stimulation from surrounding environment at residential scale
findings.quote: higher number of central markers both at the individual level of the private territory and collective level of the public territory, as in the case of Kavaklıdere district, implies higher degrees of place attachment and stimulation from the surrounding environment at the residential scale.

findings.consequent: Perceived residential territory size
findings.quote: perceived residential territory size of the respondents who own a car (M = 55.5 ha) is significantly larger than the territory size of the non-car owners (M = 39 ha).

findings.consequent: Perceived residential territory size
findings.quote: the perceived residential territory size of the individuals aged 18-24 (M = 20 ha) are significantly smaller than the size of individuals who are 25-39 (M = 53,0 ha), 40-60 (M = 53 ha) and 60+ (M = 43 ha) years old.

findings.consequent: Perceived residential territory size
findings.quote: the perceived residential territory size of the students (M = 22 ha) are significantly smaller than public employees (M = 53 ha), free lancers (M = 50,5 ha), retired respondents (M = 62 ha) and others (M = 69 ha).

findings.antecedent: Occupation (Private sector employees, Business owners) in Kavaklıdere
findings.consequent: Perceived residential territory size
findings.quote: the perceived residential territory size of private sector employees (M = 39 ha) and business owners (M = 36.5 ha) are also significantly smaller than retired (M = 62 ha) and other (M = 69 ha) occupational groups.

findings.consequent: Perceived residential territory size
findings.quote: the size of women's perceived residential territory size (M = 54 ha) is significantly smaller than that of men (M = 74 ha).

findings.antecedent: Education level (Literate/secondary school graduates) in Çukurambar
findings.consequent: Perceived residential territory size
findings.quote: The perceived residential territory size of the respondents who are literate or secondary school graduates (M = 43 ha) is significantly smaller than the size of the respondents with graduate degrees (M = 101 ha).

findings.consequent: Ability to identify landmarks
findings.quote: In Kavaklıdere District majority of the 300 respondents (70%) were able to identify a landmark in their residential area... In a similar way, majority of the 300 respondents (83%) in Çukurambar District were able to identify a landmark in their residential area

findings.consequent: Type of landmarks mentioned (buildings vs. open spaces)
findings.quote: in terms of types of landmarks; 36% mentioned a building, 32% mentioned a street... only 7% mentioned an open space as a landmark (Table 5.7). Yet, the most frequently mentioned landmarks are; Esat crossroads, Tunalı Hilmi Avenue, Kocatepe Mosque, Güven Hospital and Kuğulupark (Table 5.6 and Figure 5.17).

findings.consequent: Mode of transportation to reach activities
findings.quote: in Kavaklıdere majority of the activities are accessed on foot while in Çukurambar the prominent mode of access is by car.

findings.consequent: Intermediary zones (semi-private territories) are visually and physically separated from public territory, hard boundary markers (high walls, gated entrances), increased distances (vertical/horizontal)
findings.quote: intermediary zones, semi-private territories, in Çukurambar are both visually and physically separated from the public territory with hard elements used as boundary markers such as high walls and gated entrance areas and when combined with the increased distances between private and public territories both vertically and horizontally in the territorial organization of space creates a deaf/passive interface zone between the private and public territories.

findings.consequent: Front yards with sitting places, softer boundary markers
findings.quote: front yards with sitting places located in Kavaklıdere district and softer elements used as boundary markers provides for an active and more permeable interface zone between the private and public territories.

findings.consequent: Territorial control of private space attained by impermeable boundary markers and surveillance mechanisms
findings.quote: territorial control of the private space is attained by impermeable boundary markers, and surveillance mechanisms in Çukurambar

findings.consequent: Higher number of central markers (sitting areas, potted plants, iron gates, personalized balconies, name plates) in private territory
findings.quote: In Kavaklıdere, central markers in private territory can be listed as: sitting areas in the front-yards facing the street, potted plants used both for boundary demarcation and personalization of the entrance areas and balconies, iron gates with ornaments at the entrances as well as name plates with unique typography.

findings.antecedent: Çukurambar (contemporary residential environment), central markers in front-yards not visible from street due to boundary markers
findings.consequent: Not communicating identity/appropriation of space
findings.quote: although there are sitting places and decorations in some of the front-yards they are not visible along the street due to high fences and walls, thus they cannot be regarded as central markers used for territorial claim that radiates outward from the territory. Hence, it can be claimed that the use of central markers at individual scale of private territory is lower in Çukurambar

findings.consequent: Central markers at public scale include various forms of street art (graffiti, stair coloring, street writings)
findings.quote: At the public scale, various forms of street art can be observed in the form of graffiti, stair coloring and street writings.

findings.consequent: Scarce central markers at public scale
findings.quote: central markers at the public scale are scarce in Çukurambar

findings.antecedent: Lower number of central markers in Çukurambar at public scale
findings.consequent: Lower levels of social cohesion, spatial attachment, group identity/belonging
findings.quote: lower number of central markers in Çukurambar at the public scale indicates lower levels of social cohesion, spatial attachment and indication of group identity and belonging.

findings.consequent: Higher number of central markers (private/public) implies higher degrees of place attachment and stimulation
findings.quote: the higher number of central markers in Kavaklıdere district both at the individual level of the private territory and collective level of the public territory implies higher degrees of place attachment and stimulation from the surrounding environment at the residential scale.

findings.consequent: Walkable environment (larger sidewalks, greenery, active front yards)
findings.quote: higher amounts of strolling can be associated with the walkable environment of the district with larger sidewalks with greenery as well as active front yards

findings.antecedent: Walkable environment (larger sidewalks, greenery, active front yards) in Kavaklıdere
findings.consequent: Increased feeling of security, increased stimulation
findings.quote: larger sidewalks with greenery as well as active front yards both increasing the feeling of security as well as providing stimulation.

findings.consequent: Higher number of open-air sport activities, more use of playgrounds
findings.quote: higher number of open-air sport activities can be related to larger park areas located within the district and more use of playgrounds to the higher number of children between the 0-9 age range in Çukurambar (2304) than Kavaklıdere (1131) as well as to the higher number of married couples with children among the respondents of Çukurambar.

findings.consequent: Higher amount of strolling
findings.quote: strolling is done 15 percent more in Kavaklıdere

findings.consequent: Higher shopping activities (other than daily grocery)
findings.quote: shopping activities other than daily grocery shopping (clothing, electronics etc.) are done 19 percent more within the residential territory in Çukurambar.

findings.consequent: Higher use of residential territory for work purposes
findings.quote: The use of residential territory for work purposes is also 19 percent more in Çukurambar

findings.consequent: Higher use of residential territory for religious purposes
findings.quote: Respondents in Çukurambar district also use their residential territory 21 percent more for religious purposes which can be associated with the socio-cultural group residing as well as higher number of mosques located in the area.

findings.consequent: Higher use of private services
findings.quote: Private services (such as hairdresser, tailor etc.) are 15 percent more used in Kavaklıdere.

findings.consequent: Higher attendance to socio-cultural activities
findings.quote: Socio-cultural activities are attended 13 percent more in Kavaklıdere

findings.consequent: Higher utilization of educational facilities
findings.quote: educational facilities are 14 percent more utilized in Çukurambar

findings.consequent: Higher car-dependency in reaching activities
findings.quote: in Çukurambar the prominent mode of access is by car.

findings.consequent: Majority of activities accessed on foot
findings.quote: majority of the activities in Kavaklıdere are accessed on foot

findings.consequent: Residents perceive and use residential territory in terms of driving distances
findings.quote: Çukurambar respondents both perceive and use their residential territory in terms of driving distances

findings.consequent: Residents perceive and corporeal experience residential environment at a walking distance scale
findings.quote: Kavaklıdere the smaller areas perceived as residential territory as well as the prominent type of access to activities on foot refers to perception and corporeal experience of residential environment at a walking distance scale.

findings.consequent: Enlarging the size of the perceived area (more opportunities with car access)
findings.quote: in the case of Kavaklıdere car ownership can be enlarging the size of the perceived area since the opportunities within reach becomes higher with car access.

findings.antecedent: Older people, retired people in Kavaklıdere
findings.consequent: More dependent on and actively use near-home territories, perceive larger areas as residential territory
findings.quote: older people, especially the retired, are both more dependent and more actively using their near-home territories thus resulting in larger areas perceived as residential territory.

findings.antecedent: Respondents with graduate degrees in Çukurambar
findings.consequent: Perceive larger areas as residential territory (related to university campuses)
findings.quote: respondents with graduate degrees can be related to the university campuses located at the surrounding of the area, which are often perceived as within the residential territory

findings.consequent: Perceive smaller areas as residential territory (higher number of housewives)
findings.quote: smaller areas perceived as residential territory by woman can be a result of higher number of housewives among the respondents.

findings.consequent: Majority of boundary markers are less permeable (physically/visually) with higher walls/fences, locked/automated gates, more surveillance mechanisms
findings.quote: the majority of the boundary markers used in Çukurambar are less permeable than Kavaklıdere both physically and visually with higher walls and fences as well as locked or automated gates at the entrances. In addition to this, the use of surveillance mechanisms is also more common in Çukurambar.

findings.consequent: Softer boundary markers (lower walls, iron fences with planting)
findings.quote: lower walls and mainly iron fences with planting appear as the prominent types of boundary markers in Kavaklıdere.

findings.consequent: Entrance areas more permeable (physically/visually) (iron gates with ornaments)
findings.quote: the entrance areas are more permeable both physically and visually that are mainly in the form of iron gates with ornaments.

findings.consequent: Narrower side-yards between private territories → shorter distances between balconies/windows → inadequate privacy
findings.quote: the narrower side-yards between private territories in Kavaklıdere creates shorter distances between balconies and windows which creates inadequate spacing for providing privacy.

findings.consequent: Narrower and active front yards with softer boundary markers → enhanced defensibility through 'eyes on the street'
findings.quote: narrower and active front yards with softer boundary markers between the private and public territories enhance the defensibility of space through ‘eyes on the street’.

findings.consequent: Reflections of spatial appropriation, attachment to particular space
findings.quote: central markers, or personalization, are reflections of spatial appropriation as well as attachment to particular space (Barlas,2006).

findings.consequent: Stimulation from physical environment (through making, modifying, defending territory)
findings.quote: stimulation from the physical environment is achieved through making, modifying and defending the territory (Porteous, 1977).

findings.consequent: Higher degrees of place attachment and stimulation from surrounding environment at residential scale
findings.quote: the higher number of central markers in Kavaklıdere district both at the individual level of the private territory and collective level of the public territory implies higher degrees of place attachment and stimulation from the surrounding environment at the residential scale.

findings.consequent: Lower levels of social cohesion, spatial attachment, group identity/belonging
findings.quote: lower number of central markers in Çukurambar at the public scale indicates lower levels of social cohesion, spatial attachment and indication of group identity and belonging.

findings.antecedent: Legible layout of the environment, spatial hierarchy
findings.consequent: Positive impact on appropriation of space as a territory, enhanced frequent use, maintenance
findings.quote: the legible layout of the environment as well as spatial hierarchy has a positive impact on the appropriation of space as a territory as well as enhancing frequent use and maintenance.

findings.antecedent: Social, cultural, and class-related conditions in a residential environment
findings.consequent: Influence form, extent, and strength of territorial functioning
findings.quote: social, cultural and class related conditions in a residential environment influence the form, extent and strength of territorial functioning.
